title: AI drafts, you decide: prompts and brand voice that work

say: AI drafts, you decide. Prompts and brand voice that work.
This is the video for module one of AI for Marketing and Automation.
Tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta AI are built on large language models, or LLMs. An LLM predicts, word by word, the text that most likely fits your request.

panel.heading: It predicts words. It does not know you.
items: Predicts likely text, word by word
Great at variation and first drafts

say: It does not look up the truth, and it does not know your business unless you tell it. That one fact explains why it helps, and why it goes wrong.

say: It is strong at variation, reshaping one text for many channels, first drafts and summaries.

say: But the strategy, the facts, the final words and the responsibility stay with you. If a customer is misled, the AI wrote it is not a defence.

say: First, invented facts. A caption may claim your soap is dermatologist approved. Never publish a claim, number, price or quote you cannot prove yourself.

panel.heading: Four ways AI drafts go wrong

say: Second, outdated information, like an old price or an old platform feature. Check before posting.

panel.heading: Four ways AI drafts go wrong

say: Third, generic tone. Every post starts to sound the same.

panel.heading: Four ways AI drafts go wrong

say: Fourth, bias. Images may show only one skin tone or body type. Review everything with your real customers in mind.

say: Before choosing tools, sort your work into AI-assisted, automated and human-led. For example, Ngozi does marketing for a catering business in Ibadan. One normal week takes her 16 hours.
With AI first drafts she edits, WhatsApp Business quick replies, and AI summaries she checks, it drops to 11.5 hours. Planning offers with the owner stays human-led.
She uses 2 of the 4.5 hours saved to reply personally to bigger catering enquiries.
Thin prompts give average copy. Write a brief like you would for a human copywriter. Start with the role, the audience and the offer.

say: Ask for options that differ in a named way, then score your favourites on clarity, benefit and voice, from 1 to 5 each.

say: For example, Amaka sells shea butter in Abuja. Her winning headline scored 14. She refines it with short follow-ups, then checks that the tub size, delivery area and deadline are all true.

panel.rule: Check every fact before you publish.

say: A brand voice guide keeps every draft sounding like one person. Keep it to two pages. Choose three traits, and define each with this, not that, because adjectives alone mean different things to different people.

panel.heading: Define each trait: this, not that
left: Warm like a trusted older sister
right: DM for price on every post

say: Warm does not mean over-familiar. Proud of craft does not mean empty luxury words. Plain means prices are stated, not hidden.

panel.heading: Define each trait: this, not that
left: Warm like a trusted older sister
right: DM for price on every post

say: Put risky words on your banned list. Medical claims such as cures or heals are banned unless the product is approved for that claim. Organic and NAFDAC approved are banned unless you can show the certificate or registration number.
Never paste customer names, phone numbers or payment details into a public AI chat. Replace names with codes, as the Data Protection Act 2023 requires careful handling.
And have a fluent speaker check any Pidgin or local-language line.

panel.heading: Banned claims and private data
items: No cures, heals or treats eczema
Local-language lines checked by a speaker

say: How do you know it works? Zainab runs an adire studio in Abeokuta. She mixes 4 AI captions with 4 of her own and numbers them.

cards.d: 4 AI captions with her guide, 4 of her own from last year, numbered 1 to 8.
Which sound like Zainab? 5 of 11 marks went to AI drafts, close to half.
One AI caption used elevate your wardrobe. She bans elevate and reruns.

say: To remember. AI predicts text, it does not check facts. Never publish a claim you cannot prove. Write a full brief, ask for variations and score them. Define your voice with this, not that. And keep customer data out of public AI tools.
